APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF SEPTEMBER 1, 2020

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO TIME,
SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED EXCLUSIVELY
OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Jerry Velasco, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Items 12.9 and 16.1 have been pulled

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt to
  address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the
  Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will take a
  short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the
  event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session
  items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the
  meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public
  wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the Council shall
  allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a speaker’s time limit of 3
  minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall be under no obligation to
  respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or comments posed by a speaker or
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 1, 2020

take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond such action as the City Council may
be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized Closed Session matter pursuant to the
Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
Session Items 4.1 through 4.8.

Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
6:05 p.m. Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
approximately 7:05 pm.

City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items 4.1
through 4.4.

  General update, no final action

  NeroCanna vs. City of El Monte, Los Angeles Superior Court Case No.
  20STCP02545.

  General update, no final action

4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) – Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Anticipated Litigation –
  One (1) Matter.

  General update, no final action

4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(3) – Conference with Legal Counsel Regarding Anticipated Litigation –
  One (1) Matter.

  General update, no final action

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0

   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 1, 2020

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 6:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed Session/Short
Recess)

5.  INVOCATION:  Mayor Quintero

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Chief of Police, David Reynoso. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  Senator Susan Rubio – Thank you so much for allowing me to join you. As you may know
  we have been pretty much locked up in Sacramento it has been really intense time for us
  and I am sure you are experiencing the same thing locally. COVID-19 has really changed
  the way we do business so I wanted to take this opportunity now that session has ended. I
  wanted to call the Council and to recommit myself to working closely together with your City
  as well as my office to make sure that we are here to see if there is any need or if we can
  help you. Mayor I know we had a lengthy discussion about a possible audit I know there
  are many other Councilmembers who have reached out to me and I am thankful that the
  City looking towards transparency and very high intention that the residents get the
  transparency that they deserve so thank you for your call. I also wanted to share some
  exciting news with you I have to be very cautious because the Governor still has to sign it
  and that is the eviction moratorium. I want to start by thanking you because I know that the
  City of El Monte has done a tremendous job taking care of our residents.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries on
  matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their name
  and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to address
  the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time to
  other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.), the
  Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted agenda
  but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent meeting.
  The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration at a future
  meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member
  of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor and/or Chair.
  Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers
  but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or questions posed. The

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 1, 2020

  Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation with any
  speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the Police
  Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms of
  any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given
  by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the meeting.
  While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the action(s) or
  proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members of the public may not engage in
  behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings, including, but not
  limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the public from being heard when it is
  their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience from hearing or
  seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any person with physical
  harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an imminent threat of
  physical harm. All persons attending the meeting must adhere to the City’s policy barring
  harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry,
  physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Last week on Friday, August 28th two days from basically
  the last work day to approve a budget the budget was approved pulling $5.0 million dollars
  from our $20.0 million reserves and utilizing a one-time $8.0 million dollar bond proceed to
  get a balanced budget on a vote of three to two. I voted no because of a few reasons why
  usually the City Manager gives the Council a budget workshop this is the time for the
  Council to get a glimpse of where we are with the budget and provide direction. There was
  no budget workshop as promised by City Manager Martinez. This budget was not on
  Council directives. This is a rudimentary practice budget, mid-year budget review, next year
  budget workshop and we pass a new budget. Professional City Managers make it a point to
  seek Council direction and prioritize these discussions. The pandemic is not an excuse to
  not include the Council in the fiscal decisions of the City. Reason number three, I have
  asked for financial documents on numerous occasions regarding the state of the City
  budget and finances I have been denied very unprofessional. Here are a few agenda dates
  for your reference requesting information on the mid-year budget March 17th, March 23rd,
  and under Councilwoman Ancona’s communication on April 7th, regarding transparency on
  May 19th and June 2nd, regarding the budget on July 7th, July 21st and July 29th. Because we
  have not been given a conscientious and continuous conversation on the fiscal state of the
  City I don’t have confidence in this budget. Therefore, due to the lack of communication
  from our City Management on Friday during budget discussions I requested a high risk
  local government agency audit essentially a State audit to be pursued by the City and we
  will be pursuing this with our State Officials. This is not the first time our City Manager Alma
  Martinez has gone through a State audit as her previous City of Lynwood underwent an
  audit which found several violations. Finally I have asked for fiscal transparency that
  documents requested from a governing Councilmember be granted and for a formal State
  audit to do a forensic review of the City’s finances. As your Councilwoman it is my fiduciary
  duty to ask the questions to protect your tax dollars and in the name of good governance of
  the City administration to provide it.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT: No material submitted.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Quintero

  Thank you all I wanted to have this experience of meeting via zoom so that I can
  understand and appreciate what it is like to be on this end and not be at the Council
  Chambers. I have to tell you I found it to be very okay I mean it was fine, I could
  hear everything, I could participate, I could even share the meeting from remote. I
  found it to be acceptable in every sense of the word we can work on the
  communication a little bit for the public comment but I can tell you I tried speaking at
  the Rio Hondo College Board meeting and I couldn’t speak if I didn’t put a public
  comment card two hours in advance so I think we have a lot more accessibility than
  I think we even give ourselves credit for. I also want to thank Senator Rubio for
  coming to speak with us. I did reach out to her she did mention to me that she was
  having trouble with communication so she did want me to share that the Legislative
  year has ended and therefore an audit is not possible this year. I did reach out to
  hear to speak to hear about that possibility as well she is going work with us during
  the next session to see what we can do to facilitate something of that sort because
  at the end of the day we all want to make sure that everyone feels comfortable with
  the transparency that is happening in our City and I can tell you very directly that
  wasn’t the case ten years ago. I remember distinctly what it was like when they
  found money it wasn’t allocated or wasn’t there and there was a lot of mistrust with
  the bargaining units and the City Manager and the staff. I mentioned earlier about
  procurement process that was not done appropriately so there were a lot of things
  that were happening at the time and so I take offense when I hear some of the
  comments that are being made about the transparency or lack of transparency or
  bringing allegations related to another City it really is comical at this point but I
  understand I get it because this is the time of the year on an election year when
  people are trying to make points and make comments that hopefully ring true to the
  community. I get that we experienced that five years ago in July of 2015 when
  Councilmembers left the dais and made statements that were inappropriate as well
  that’s just part of unfortunately this process but as I have said over and over again I
  have total and absolute confidence in the residents of this community and the voters
  of this community to do always what they believe in their best judgement is the right
  thing to do and I trust that and have confidence in that. As someone who used to
  prosecute cases and had to work with jurors who were members of the public I
  always had confidence that they would come out with the right verdict and it may
  not have been the verdict that I want but I knew they would always come out with a
  just verdict. I felt that strongly then and I continue to feel that throughout all these
  years of service in the City of El Monte. So I just want to leave you guys with those
  thoughts. Thank you very much we had a very good meeting.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Morales

  18B.1 Update Regarding El Monte Slow Streets in Collaboration with Active San
  Gabriel Valley.

  I am grateful to Active SGV for their collaboration and their work in redesigning
  walkable spaces throughout the City. I have been able to take some strolls now

  11
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 1, 2020

  that we are home and we are having an opportunity to explore more of the City now
  as we are going through this COVID situation. I just wanted to say thank you to
  Active SGV for the work that they are doing in the redesign and the collaboration
  with the City I think that the designs that are coming up and the surveys were sent
  out to the community people definitely help us improve walkable environments so
  that if we can have spaces where our children, our families can take nice strolls
  without having the fear of vehicles zooming by too fast. Again their safety is our
  priority. Secondly, we are working on the opening of both parks and in particular the
  skate park is really close to my heart so I am really happy that we are moving on
  finally opening it up for our community. I know there is a huge demand for this
  skate park as well as the doggie park and that staff is definitely moving in making
  sure that we have those spaces open as quickly as possible. I am also looking
  forward to making sure that we collaborate with Senator Rubio with whatever way
  we can particularly in the two items that she mentioned where we are working
  toward protecting our community from eviction particularly knowing that this
  recession may take us longer to recover than we would hope and renters in our
  community absolutely need the protection staring at the State level and all the way
  down to the County and the City level.

  18B.2 Update Regarding Citywide Broadband Accessibility.

18C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  I am echoing on Councilwoman Martinez Muela’s sentiments in regards to our
  technology there has to be a better way to listen to those who are calling for public
  comment or as Senator Rubio called in as well some of the stuff she said was hard
  to hear. Currently we have a microphone at the end of an iPad I don’t think that is
  the best technological way to do this there has to be a better way for people to
  conference in. I know when Councilmember Martinez Muela and I were zooming in
  it wasn’t cutting it so there has to be a better way and I encourage staff to look into it
  to improve this process. In regards to the deferment of the car allowance on Friday
  the majority of the Council voted to defer City Council car allowance I want to
  ensure that it is for all elected officials including the Treasurer and City Clerk and
  that it is worked in as part as the budget savings that had been proposed.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  18D.1 Discussion Regarding Public Comment Process.

  I have realized that during COVID there were a lot of considerations myself included
  staying home and sheltering in place was really important to me and my family but I
  really do feel like COVID has taken its toll on our governing processes including
  citizen participation. I think we have done what we needed to do at the time but I
  know that there are cities that are doing more effective processes that allow more
  participation from the public and not a summary read by the Mayor or the City Clerk
  but actually being able to hear directly from our community members. The request
  is to have staff seek out maybe a couple of other processes to better what we got
  going on here in the City of El Monte allowing our community to have their voices be
  heard even if that means that they eventually get to come to City Hall and be

  12
   City Council Meeting Minutes of September 1, 2020

  present with their mask on whatever that looks like it feels as though it is time to
  start hearing from our community directly and in real time. Yes there is the common
  call line but I can tell you that there is nothing better than being able to be in person
  and be able to address Council and be able to see your faces as we are sharing our
  concerns. On the zoom calls it is really hard to hear these residents not only was it
  hard to hear this last resident, it was hard to hear Senator Rubio and I want to make
  sure there is a more clear process and a direct line to general public comment and
  communication.

  18D.2 Discussion Regarding ADA Access to Meetings.

  The request from a community member who does have ADA considerations was
  that the notice be changed or made more bold so that the ADA access conversation
  which is here be put more prominently on the agenda so that they know how and
  when and where they can contact City Hall if they would like to participate in the
  governing process. With that I just want to say welcome to September and
  community we thank you for just being so diligent in staying home, staying safe God
  willing we will be able to get this City opened up soon. I hope you have been
  enjoying the air dining as much as I have that should be a goal of us as a City and
  as a City Council to find more ways to continue the Al Fresco Dining here in our
  City. So with that thank you for letting me be your Councilmember I appreciate it.

18E.  Councilman Velasco

  18E.1 Update Regarding Mini Pitch Soccer Fields.

  Did not discuss.

  18E.2 Update Regarding the Weekly COVID-19 Testing for El Monte Residents.

  As we announced before we are having free testing for residents. If you have
  insurance they will accept that all you need is a social security number to give to
  them. People are being tested and they are not being charged. It is every other
  Thursday.

  18E.3 Update Regarding the El Monte Free COVID-19 Youth Learn and Care
